why-some-woods-drink-and-some-spit.file: Piece of oak wood from the ship Vasa 4.jpg
why-some-woods-drink-and-some-spit.alt: Oak wood sample showing ring-porous structure that absorbs finishing coats
why-some-woods-drink-and-some-spit.caption: Ring-porous oak moves finish into vessels; always test absorption on scrap from the same board.
why-some-woods-drink-and-some-spit.credit_label: Wikimedia Commons — Piece of oak wood from the ship Vasa 4

linseed-oil-polymerizes.alt: Flax Linum usitatissimum plants source of linseed drying oil for wood finishes
linseed-oil-polymerizes.caption: Linseed oil is pressed from flax; polymerization in the shop still needs thin coats and air.

shellac-is-a-bug-resin.alt: Natural shellac resin in blonde amber and garnet grades before mixing with alcohol
shellac-is-a-bug-resin.caption: Shellac colour grades are refining choices, not different bugs — dissolve in alcohol and brush.

grain-raise-is-swelling.file: Surface wooden furniture interior design texture.jpg
grain-raise-is-swelling.alt: Wood furniture surface texture where raised grain shows after wetting
grain-raise-is-swelling.caption: Raised grain reads as whiskers after a wetting step; knock back before stain or topcoat.
grain-raise-is-swelling.credit_label: Wikimedia Commons — Surface wooden furniture texture

milk-paint-is-casein-and-lime.alt: Casein milk protein precipitate the binder chemistry behind traditional milk paint
milk-paint-is-casein-and-lime.caption: Milk paint is casein chemistry, not acrylic in a rustic label — protein sets the chalky film.

oil-on-teak-rosewood-and-other-greasy-ci.alt: Teak Tectona grandis tree oily exotic species common in furniture shops
oil-on-teak-rosewood-and-other-greasy-ci.caption: Teak and rosewood families carry extractives; solvent wipe and test coat before the show face.

sanding-decides-the-film.alt: Sandpaper grit closeup showing scratch pattern left before furniture finish
sanding-decides-the-film.caption: Coarser grit telegraphs through thin shellac; last sand sets the sheen baseline.

french-polish-without-the-monastery.file: Me applying varnish to the wood.jpg
french-polish-without-the-monastery.alt: Shop worker applying thin varnish coat with pad on wood not staged hazmat
french-polish-without-the-monastery.caption: Pad and brush work is thin passes — French polish is shellac layers, not one flooded coat.
french-polish-without-the-monastery.credit_label: Wikimedia Commons — Applying varnish to wood

waterborne-means-emulsion.alt: Water-based latex paint bucket showing milky emulsion before coalescence on wood
waterborne-means-emulsion.caption: Milky in the container is dispersed polymer; clarity comes after water leaves and film knits.

a-staged-dining-table-schedule.alt: Wooden dining table top where multi-day finish schedule matters before delivery
a-staged-dining-table-schedule.caption: Dining tables need staged sealer and topcoat days; do not book dinner before full cure.

spar-varnish-and-porch-chalk.alt: Spar varnish can for exterior wood not interior table film
spar-varnish-and-porch-chalk.caption: Spar formulas flex and chalk outdoors; interior tops usually want a harder alkyd or PU film.

what-a-finish-actually-is.alt: Aged wood plank surface showing pores and wear a finish must slow
what-a-finish-actually-is.caption: A finish slows dirt and moisture on fiber like this; shine is what light does afterward.
